pin_variations.title: Make-Ahead Creamy Brussels Sprouts Protein Snack for Busy Days
pin_variations.description: Meal prep made simple! This creamy Brussels sprouts recipe is low calorie but high in protein, perfect for busy afternoons or post-gym fuel. It keeps well and tastes great chilled. Pin it for your snack stash! 🥗💚 #MealPrep #HighProtein #LowCalorie

ingredients: 3 cups fresh Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
1/2 cup zero-fat Greek yogurt (0% fat), plain
1/2 teaspoon xanthan gum (optional, for creaminess and thickening)
yield: Approximately 1 large bowl per serving, 6 snack servings, about 2 cups volume per serving
introduction: I’ve always struggled with feeling hungry on low-calorie days, especially when I’m trying to cut but still want to eat a decent amount of food. Tiny snack portions just don’t cut it for me, and I hate feeling like I’m starving between meals. That’s why I started experimenting with volume eating — snacks that fill your stomach but don’t pack on the calories. This creamy Brussels sprouts recipe is a game changer. It’s got way more food volume than those tiny protein bars, and it’s surprisingly creamy without any added fats. The trick? Whipping chilled egg whites to add fluff and volume, plus a little zero-fat Greek yogurt for tang and protein. I also add xanthan gum to keep it thick and luscious without any oil or cream. It’s perfect for when I need a filling snack post-workout or during that afternoon slump. I remember my first batch was too watery because I skipped the xanthan gum, so don’t make that mistake! Now I have this snack almost every day, and even my friends ask how I eat so much and still lose weight. The portion looks huge but clocks in under 150 calories with over 20 grams of protein, so you can eat big and stay on track.

instructions.instruction: Start by trimming and halving the Brussels sprouts. You want them fresh and raw to keep the fiber intact, which adds volume and crunch. If you prefer, you can lightly steam them for 1-2 minutes to soften slightly, but raw keeps the snack crisp and low calorie. Avoid overcooking here because mushy sprouts will reduce the satisfying texture. The fiber and water content in raw sprouts help fill you up without adding calories, making this snack perfect for volume eating.
instructions.doneness_cue: Brussels sprouts are crisp and bright green, not wilted or soggy

instructions.instruction: Pour the chilled liquid egg whites into a mixing bowl and whip them with a hand mixer until soft peaks form. This aeration adds volume and fluffiness without fat or calories. Whipping egg whites properly is key to achieving a creamy texture later. Don’t overbeat or the whites will become dry and grainy, but underbeating won’t give you enough lift. The cold temperature helps stabilize the foam, so keep your egg whites chilled for best results.
instructions.doneness_cue: Soft, billowy peaks that hold shape but still slightly droop

instructions.instruction: In a separate bowl, mix the zero-fat Greek yogurt with lemon juice, Dijon mustard, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. This mix provides tang, flavor, and creaminess while keeping calories low. The acidity from lemon juice helps cut through the earthiness of Brussels sprouts and prevents the protein powder or yogurt from tasting chalky. Whisk until smooth and well combined.
instructions.doneness_cue: Smooth, creamy dressing with no lumps and a bright, tangy aroma

instructions.instruction: If using xanthan gum, sprinkle it evenly over the yogurt mixture and whisk quickly to avoid clumps. Xanthan gum acts as a zero-calorie thickener, giving the snack a luscious, creamy texture that mimics fat without adding calories. It also helps bind the mixture so it doesn’t separate. This step is optional but highly recommended for a satisfying mouthfeel.
instructions.doneness_cue: Dressing thickens slightly and clump-free after whisking

instructions.instruction: Gently fold the whipped egg whites into the yogurt dressing in thirds, using a spatula to keep as much air as possible. This folding technique preserves the fluffiness, which is what makes the snack feel so voluminous and light. Avoid stirring vigorously or you’ll deflate the egg whites and lose that airy texture. The goal is a creamy, fluffy mixture that coats the Brussels sprouts without weighing them down.
instructions.doneness_cue: Mixture looks smooth, creamy, and fluffy with no large lumps

instructions.instruction: Add the halved Brussels sprouts to the creamy mixture and fold gently until all are coated evenly. The sprouts provide crunch and fiber, while the creamy dressing adds protein and tang. Mixing thoroughly ensures every bite has flavor and texture contrast, which helps keep you satisfied longer.
instructions.doneness_cue: All Brussels sprouts are evenly coated in the creamy dressing

instructions.instruction: Taste and adjust seasoning with extra salt, pepper, or lemon juice if needed. Because this snack is low fat, seasoning is key to making it flavorful and enjoyable. Don’t be shy with the lemon or mustard; they brighten the whole dish and prevent blandness.
instructions.doneness_cue: Balanced, bright flavor with a slight tang and savory notes

instructions.instruction: Chill the creamy Brussels sprouts snack in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before serving. Chilling helps the flavors meld and firms up the texture, especially since there’s no fat to bind the ingredients. If you skip chilling, the snack may feel watery and less satisfying.
instructions.doneness_cue: Snack is firmed up but still creamy and fresh tasting

instructions.instruction: Serve chilled as a snack or light meal. Portion into 6 servings for easy grab-and-go snacks. This recipe keeps well in an airtight container for up to 3 days, making it perfect for meal prep. The volume and protein content help keep hunger at bay without adding extra calories.
instructions.doneness_cue: Snack holds shape in container and looks fresh and creamy

why_this_recipe_works.section: Why This Creamy Brussels Sprouts Snack Fills You Up Without the Calories
why_this_recipe_works.content:
This snack works because it combines several nutritional and culinary tricks to maximize fullness while minimizing calories. First, protein has a high thermic effect of food (TEF), meaning your body burns more calories digesting protein than carbs or fats. This also triggers satiety hormones like PYY and GLP-1, which help you feel full longer. By using egg whites and zero-fat Greek yogurt, this recipe packs over 20 grams of protein per serving with very little fat or calories.

Second, the use of high-volume, low-calorie ingredients like Brussels sprouts adds fiber and water, stretching your stomach and sending mechanical fullness signals to your brain. This volume eating approach tricks your body into feeling satisfied without overeating. The fiber also slows digestion, promoting steady energy.

Third, texture plays a huge role in satisfaction. The whipped egg whites aerate the snack, creating a fluffy, creamy mouthfeel without fat. Xanthan gum helps mimic the richness of fat, preventing watery separation common in low-fat mixtures. The acidity from lemon juice and mustard cuts through any chalkiness from protein, balancing flavor and enhancing palatability.

Finally, the large portion size and bright flavors psychologically satisfy cravings, making it easier to stick to a calorie deficit. The snack’s creamy yet crunchy contrast keeps eating interesting, which is crucial when you’re trying to avoid boredom on a diet.

ingredient_notes.liquid egg whites: Look for pasteurized liquid egg whites with no added preservatives or sodium for the cleanest flavor. Liquid whites whip better when cold, so keep them refrigerated until use. They provide pure protein with almost zero calories and create volume without fat. Avoid powdered egg whites here, as they don’t aerate as well and can add chalkiness.
ingredient_notes.zero-fat Greek yogurt: Choose plain 0% fat Greek yogurt with no added sugars or thickeners. This ingredient adds protein and creaminess while keeping calories low. Greek yogurt’s natural acidity helps prevent protein powder chalkiness and balances flavors. Avoid 2% or full-fat versions as they increase calories and change texture.
ingredient_notes.Brussels sprouts: Fresh, firm Brussels sprouts work best for crunch and fiber. Avoid wilted or yellowing sprouts, which are less flavorful and have lower nutrient density. Raw sprouts provide maximum volume and fiber, essential for fullness. Light steaming is optional but can reduce crunch and calorie-burning fiber content.
ingredient_notes.xanthan gum: This zero-calorie hydrocolloid thickens and stabilizes the creamy mixture, mimicking fat’s mouthfeel without added calories. Use sparingly to avoid gummy texture. It prevents watery separation common in low-fat dairy and protein powder blends, improving creaminess and texture.
ingredient_notes.lemon juice: Fresh lemon juice adds acidity that brightens flavor and helps mask any chalkiness from protein powder or yogurt. It also balances the earthiness of Brussels sprouts. Bottled lemon juice can be used but fresh is preferred for the best taste and aroma.

pro_tips.tip: Always use chilled egg whites and whip them cold to maximize volume and fluffiness.
pro_tips.reason: Cold egg whites hold air better when whipped, producing a stable foam that adds volume without fat. If egg whites are warm, they won’t whip properly and the snack will lack that airy, creamy texture essential for feeling full without extra calories.

pro_tips.tip: Add xanthan gum slowly while whisking to avoid clumps and ensure smooth thickening.
pro_tips.reason: Xanthan gum can clump quickly if added all at once. Whisking it in gradually disperses the powder evenly, preventing lumps and giving a consistent creamy texture. This step is crucial for low-fat snacks where texture can otherwise be watery or grainy.

pro_tips.tip: Don’t overmix the whipped egg whites into the yogurt mixture to keep the snack light and fluffy.
pro_tips.reason: Vigorous mixing deflates the air bubbles in whipped egg whites, resulting in a denser, less satisfying snack. Gentle folding preserves the aeration, which is key to volume eating and satiety in a low-calorie snack.

common_mistakes_to_avoid.mistake: Skipping xanthan gum and ending up with a watery, separated snack.
common_mistakes_to_avoid.why_it_happens: People often think xanthan gum is optional, but without it, the low-fat yogurt and egg whites separate and lose creaminess. This ruins texture and satisfaction.
common_mistakes_to_avoid.fix: Add just 1/2 teaspoon xanthan gum while whisking the yogurt mixture. This binds water and protein, creating a stable, creamy texture that holds together well.

common_mistakes_to_avoid.mistake: Using full-fat yogurt or adding oils, which increases calories significantly.
common_mistakes_to_avoid.why_it_happens: Many assume creaminess requires fat, so they add full-fat dairy or oils, which defeats the low-calorie purpose.
common_mistakes_to_avoid.fix: Stick to 0% fat Greek yogurt and rely on whipped egg whites and xanthan gum for creaminess without extra calories.

common_mistakes_to_avoid.mistake: Overwhipping egg whites until dry or grainy, causing a chalky mouthfeel.
common_mistakes_to_avoid.why_it_happens: Overbeating removes moisture from whites, making them stiff and less pleasant in texture.
common_mistakes_to_avoid.fix: Stop whipping when soft peaks form. The whites should hold shape but still be moist and fluffy.

variations.name: Spicy Sriracha Creamy Brussels Sprouts
variations.description: Add 1 tablespoon of sugar-free sriracha sauce to the yogurt dressing for a spicy kick. This variation adds flavor without calories and pairs well with the creamy texture. Macros remain similar, with a tiny calorie bump from the sauce.
variations.technical_note: Mix sriracha into the yogurt mixture before folding in egg whites to ensure even distribution of heat.

variations.name: Lemon Herb Creamy Brussels Sprouts
variations.description: Stir in fresh chopped dill and parsley along with lemon zest for a bright, herbal twist. This adds freshness and depth without affecting calories or protein. The texture stays creamy and fluffy.
variations.technical_note: Add herbs to the yogurt dressing before folding in whipped egg whites to keep flavors balanced.

variations.name: Smoky Paprika Brussels Sprouts Snack
variations.description: Sprinkle smoked paprika and a pinch of cumin into the dressing for a smoky flavor profile. This low-calorie spice addition enhances taste and keeps the snack interesting. Protein and calories stay consistent.
variations.technical_note: Incorporate spices in the yogurt dressing step for even flavor infusion.

variations.name: Vegan Variation with Aquafaba
variations.description: Replace egg whites with 3/4 cup aquafaba (chickpea water) whipped to soft peaks and use coconut yogurt (unsweetened, low-fat) instead of Greek yogurt. Expect slightly lower protein but similar volume and creaminess.
variations.technical_note: Whip aquafaba longer than egg whites to achieve stable peaks; texture will be lighter and less dense.

variations.name: Add Protein Powder Boost
variations.description: Mix 1 scoop unflavored or vanilla whey isolate protein powder into the yogurt dressing for extra protein. This increases protein grams per serving to around 25g with minimal calorie increase.
variations.technical_note: Blend protein powder thoroughly with yogurt and lemon juice to prevent chalkiness before folding in egg whites.

nutrition.note: Nutritional values are estimates and may vary based on specific ingredients and protein powder used. Always calculate based on your specific brands. This recipe is designed for a high-protein, low-calorie approach.

storage_and_reheating.room_temperature: This snack should not be kept at room temperature for more than 1 hour due to the egg whites and yogurt. Keep covered to prevent drying out. Warm temperatures can cause separation and loss of volume.
storage_and_reheating.refrigerator: Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days. The snack firms up nicely when chilled and flavors meld. It tastes best cold or at room temperature after a few minutes out of the fridge.
storage_and_reheating.freezer: Freezing is not recommended as the texture of whipped egg whites and yogurt will degrade, becoming watery and grainy upon thawing.
storage_and_reheating.reheating: This snack is best eaten cold or at room temperature. Reheating can cause separation and loss of fluffiness, so avoid heating.
storage_and_reheating.make_ahead_strategy: You can prepare the Brussels sprouts and yogurt dressing up to 2 days ahead, storing separately. Whip egg whites fresh and fold together just before eating to maintain maximum volume and freshness.

faq.question: Can I use powdered egg whites instead of liquid for this recipe?
faq.answer: Powdered egg whites can be used but they don’t whip as well as liquid ones, often resulting in a denser texture. If you use powder, rehydrate it fully and whip it cold, but expect less volume and fluffiness compared to fresh liquid whites.

faq.question: How do I prevent the snack from tasting chalky with protein powder?
faq.answer: To avoid chalkiness, blend protein powder thoroughly with acidic ingredients like lemon juice and yogurt before folding in egg whites. The acidity helps break down protein powder texture, and chilling the mixture also improves mouthfeel.

faq.question: Is this snack suitable for cutting or calorie deficit diets?
faq.answer: Absolutely! With under 150 calories and over 20 grams of protein per serving, this snack keeps you full without excess calories, making it ideal for cutting phases or calorie deficit diets.

faq.question: Can I substitute Greek yogurt with regular yogurt?
faq.answer: Regular yogurt usually has more sugar and less protein, which will lower the protein content and increase calories. If you must substitute, choose plain, non-fat yogurt and adjust macros accordingly.

faq.question: What if I don’t have xanthan gum? Can I skip it?
faq.answer: You can skip xanthan gum but expect a thinner, more watery texture that separates faster. To compensate, serve immediately after mixing and consume quickly for best texture.

faq.question: How long does this snack keep its fluffy texture after mixing?
faq.answer: It stays fluffy for several hours when chilled, but will slowly deflate if left at room temperature. For best volume, eat within 24 hours and store covered in the fridge.

faq.question: Can I add other vegetables to this snack?
faq.answer: Yes! Low-calorie, crunchy veggies like celery or cucumber can be mixed in for extra volume and texture without adding many calories.

faq.question: Is it safe to eat raw egg whites in this recipe?
faq.answer: Using pasteurized liquid egg whites is safe and eliminates the risk of salmonella. Avoid raw whole eggs or unpasteurized whites.
